who: Founder with a finished 1,100-line product spec who wants to build the product with Claude Code
pain: Worried that building a large spec in one go will lose context and produce sloppy output; asks the community how to split the implementation of the whole product into portions
workaround: Splitting the spec into portions with one git worktree per portion

who: Developer with an existing repo (NestJS service plus Python automation worker for CNC machining) using a Cursor long-running agent
pain: Asks the agent for a gap analysis and an incremental MVP-to-v2 plan with module boundaries for the existing repo; plan depth is inconsistent and needs back-and-forth, and the 80+ hour run still needed follow-up work
workaround: Has a stronger model draft the plan first, then feeds it to the long-running agent to produce the final plan

who: Claude user writing a book with Claude's help
pain: Hits the session usage limit repeatedly; Claude compacts the long conversation at the start of each session and compaction eats most of the new session's usage before chapter work resumes

who: Developer working in a TypeScript monorepo with 200+ files
pain: Claude keeps hitting context limits when it needs module relationships for refactoring work; chunking and separate chats do not feel smooth
workaround: Chunking the code, separate chats per area, and a self-written context manager

who: Vibe coder building features with Claude Code
pain: Context window fills mid-feature, forcing a wrap-up and handoff to a new session; momentum is lost and the next session starts confused if anything was not captured
workaround: Manually writes a summary to a CONTINUE.md file, opens a new session and re-injects the context

who: Cursor user who asked the agent to implement a refactoring
pain: Agent started modifying files for a large refactor, then stopped early without meeting all requirements; wants agents that can carry large refactors or big features to the end

who: Engineer on a team planning a major refactor that must reproduce existing output one for one
pain: Unsure what instructions and guidelines to put in the initial prompt so a long-running agent completes a large refactor and the result is usable

who: Developer building an operational dashboard with 8 feature tracks, using Claude Code sub-agents to analyze the codebase before planning each track
pain: Planning each new feature through parallel sub-agents fails because they share the parent token budget and hit output limits, so planning takes 2-3 hours instead of 30 minutes
workaround: Sub-agents write analysis to files and return short summaries; runs them sequentially or in separate terminals by hand

who: Developer running a multi-session project with milestone progress tracked in CLAUDE.md
pain: Every new session needs a manual prompt to read the project status and find the next milestone, which breaks flow across sessions
workaround: Manually asks Claude to check the CLAUDE.md file and identify the next task at the start of each session

who: Game developer using Claude Code Desktop on Windows to build a multi-file pet house system
pain: Large build tasks fill the context after about 30 minutes, 3-4 times per task, forcing a manual handoff to a new conversation that costs about 5 minutes each time
workaround: Has Claude save progress to a knowledge-base file, then pastes a handoff message into a new conversation by hand

who: Developer who gives Claude one feature or refactor task at a time on their own projects
pain: Cannot see how to split their own project work into parallel pieces; an earlier attempt with parallel agents caused heavy merge and testing overhead
workaround: Runs one task at a time and reviews and cleans up afterwards

who: Builder of a product platform using Claude Code and Codex
pain: Usage limits interrupt multi-hour debugging; ends up spending more time planning around limits than fixing the problem
workaround: Switches between tools, stops completely, or plans sessions around limit resets
